requested_changes.problem: Stage vectors are checked for drift=[] and integer revision/count, but their revision and count are not joined to the exact Ledger.add prefix that existed at that stage. Final add-chain equality does not establish before-case closure.
requested_changes.evidence: check_vector(path, expected_count=None) accepts any integer revision and positive count when no count is supplied. Controller before/after vectors at line100 and pre-build/compile/final vectors at line130 call it without an expected count. Lines131-139 separately reconstruct the final add chain, without consuming stage revisions. Worker line111 checks final cardinality only, not the exact initial member set or stage revision.

static_counterexample.mutation: Change only one controller stage vector revision to -1 or a nonexisting future integer, or file_count to1, while leaving drift=[] and the final valid add chain unchanged.
static_counterexample.reason: Existing local predicates do not relate those fields to the valid prefix. This is a source-level acceptance-gap argument, not a recorded runtime result.

required_prefix_contract: Reconstruct a revision-indexed cumulative map from every Ledger.add event, including zero-new-file events. Reject missing/duplicate/out-of-range revisions and inconsistent totals.

Validate add-event group order and permissible additions against the unchanged producer stages. Bind every before/after/pre-build/compile/final vector to its exact expected revision and cardinality; final vector must use the last complete prefix.

Compare exact path/hash/bytes membership, with the same collision normalization rules, rather than only counts. Each consumed authority/resource/source must occur in the prefix before the stage using it.
Join case request.allowed_module_files to its exact case-before prefix; reject omissions, additions or equal-cardinality substitutions.
Reconstruct outer and worker own add chains and bind their before/after vectors to the intended immutable request/authority/resource membership, not just len(final).

Validate timestamp shape and producer-consistent ordering where timestamps are already recorded; timestamps alone cannot replace exact group/member joins. Do not invent lifecycle proof from Python point-time observations.

Retain checks for every owned result, exact argv/roster, raw PASS/no SKIP, runtime sources/modules, closed-copy proof, generated compiler inputs and complete output manifest. Do not relax a prior guard to obtain readiness.
